record.field: E-Commerce Platform
ECOM-2026

Full-featured B2C e-commerce platform for Nguyen Trading Company, replacing their legacy catalog system. The platform will serve 50,000+ registered customers with a modern shopping experience, integrated payment gateways (VNPay, MoMo, bank transfer), and a real-time inventory management system.

Key deliverables:

  • Responsive web storefront (React.js + Next.js)
  • RESTful API backend (Python/FastAPI)
  • Admin dashboard for product and order management
  • VNPay & MoMo payment gateway integration
  • Elasticsearch-powered product search
  • Automated order fulfillment notifications

Product images not displaying on iOS Safari 17
in_progress
major
iOS 17.4, Safari 17 — iPhone 14 Pro / iPhone 15
Product images on both the listing page and detail page are showing broken image icons on iOS Safari 17. The issue does not occur on Chrome for iOS or on desktop Safari.

1. Open product listing page on iPhone (iOS 17.4) using Safari browser. 2. Observe that all product images are displayed as broken image icons. 3. Open the same URL on Chrome for iOS — images display correctly. 4. Network tab shows 403 Forbidden responses for image CDN URLs in Safari.
Product images should display correctly on all browsers including iOS Safari, matching the appearance on desktop Chrome.

All product images show broken image icons on iOS Safari 17. Network inspection reveals 403 Forbidden errors from the Cloudflare R2 CDN. Suspected cause: Safari's cross-origin cookie handling with CDN signed URLs.
Elasticsearch returns zero results for Vietnamese diacritic queries
confirmed
critical
Staging — Elasticsearch 8.12, Python 3.11

When customers search using fully-diacriticized Vietnamese words (e.g., "áo thun" or "giày dép"), the search returns zero results even though products with matching names exist in the index. Searching without diacritics (e.g., "ao thun") returns correct results.
1. Go to product search bar. 2. Type "áo thun" (T-shirt in Vietnamese with tone marks). 3. Observe zero results are returned. 4. Type "ao thun" (without diacritics) — correct products appear.
Search should return relevant products for both diacriticized ("áo thun") and non-diacriticized ("ao thun") Vietnamese queries.
Diacriticized Vietnamese search returns zero results. The icu_folding token filter is configured but the query analyzer does not apply the same folding to search terms.
Category filter selection is reset when navigating to page 2
new
minor
Production — Chrome 124, Windows 11
When a user selects one or more category filters on the product listing page and then clicks to page 2, all selected filters are reset and the page shows unfiltered results.

1. Go to /products page. 2. Select 2 or more category checkboxes in the filter sidebar. 3. Products are filtered correctly on page 1. 4. Click the "Next page" button or page 2 in pagination. 5. Filters are cleared and all products (unfiltered) appear on page 2.
Selected filters should persist across pagination pages. URL should reflect both active filters and page number.
Filter state is lost on pagination. The URL shows ?page=2 but category filter params are dropped. This is a state management bug in the React pagination component.
API response timeout when listing products with 1000+ records
in_progress
major
Staging — PostgreSQL 16, 1,200 product records loaded

The GET /api/v1/products endpoint times out (30s) when the product database has more than 1,000 records. The response time grows from ~80ms (100 products) to 32,000ms (1,200 products) — a non-linear performance degradation.

1. Load 1,200 product records into staging database using the seed script. 2. Call GET /api/v1/products?page=1&page_size=24. 3. Observe the request takes over 30 seconds and returns a 504 Gateway Timeout.
Product listing API should respond in under 500ms regardless of total product count in the database, using proper SQL indexing and query optimization.
Query execution plan shows a full table scan on the products table with no index on the sorting column (created_at). Adding an index on (category_id, created_at) should resolve the issue.
Login session expires prematurely on mobile browsers
resolved
major
Staging — Chrome Mobile 124, Android 13 / iOS 17

Root cause: The JWT refresh token expiry was incorrectly set to 1 hour instead of 30 days in the production environment config. Fixed by correcting the REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS environment variable and deploying the updated .env.production. Verified in staging — session now persists for 30 days with automatic token refresh on active sessions.
Logged-in users on mobile browsers are being logged out after approximately 1 hour of inactivity, even though the expected session duration is 30 days.
1. Log in on Chrome Mobile (Android). 2. Leave the app idle for 65 minutes. 3. Open the app — redirected to login page. 4. Expected: user should remain logged in for 30 days.
User should remain logged in for 30 days with automatic token refresh on activity.
Session expires after ~1 hour. JWT refresh token had incorrect expiry set in staging environment variables.
